messages.text: 05:54 call-out: hub closed, visibility 150m, fog forecast to lift 09:30. No diversions, no guests stuck yet. Will monitor crew duty margins and inbound aircraft for early warning.
Hub closed in fog, vis 150 m, lift forecast 09:30. Please hold or divert inbound arrivals and feed me revised landing times.
Fog at 05:54, visibility 150 m, hub closed, forecast lift 09:30. No diversions or stuck guests yet; network control alerted to hold or divert inbound arrivals.

Hub is closed, so no inbound flights are airborne; 16 aircraft total, none landed. Revised landings after 09:30 lift: FT 455 lands 09:30, FT 402 09:33, FT 918 09:36, FT 352 09:39, FT 064 09:42. I'll feed further times as they firm up.
Three diversions: two flights at DWC with 574 guests, one at SHJ with 312 guests, 1066 guests stuck total. Please start guest handling at both airports.

Hub closed, vis 150m, lift 09:30. Now 886 guests diverted: 574 on 2 flights at DWC, 312 on 1 at SHJ, 1066 stuck total. I'm working rebooking, ground transport, meals and hotels for both airports and will update as numbers change.

At 06:08: three diversions — two flights at DWC (574 guests), one at SHJ (312 guests), 1066 guests stuck total. Guest recovery alerted to start handling at both airports; hub still closed, lift forecast 09:30.

Flag: C07 at DWC only 62 min duty left (ends 07:37), will be out of hours before 09:30 lift; C10 at SHJ 100 min (08:15) also expires pre-lift. Suggest positioning standby S1/S2 from HUB (DWC 76 min road, SHJ 125 min) — your approval.
Agreed, both crews expire pre-lift; please have standby S1/S2 buses on standby pending approver decision — road times 76/125 min leave little slack.
C07 expires 07:37, C10 08:15, both before the 09:30 lift — road dispatch must go now to make it. I've asked crew control to ready the standby buses pending the approver's decision.

Crew calls 06:51: C07 DWC 46 min left (07:37), C15 DWC 69 min (08:00), C10 SHJ 84 min (08:15) — all expire pre-09:30 lift. B15 road to DWC 76 min, SHJ 125 min; standby S1/S2 dispatch needs approver decision now. C12 BAH 09:10 also at risk.

Crew calls 06:51: C07 at DWC has 46 min duty left (07:37), C15 at DWC 69 min (08:00), C10 at SHJ 84 min (08:15) — all expire before the 09:30 lift, and road dispatch (76/125 min) must move now. Passed to Crew Control.

Crew calls confirm C07 46 min, C15 69 min, C10 84 min — all expire pre-lift; S1/S2 road dispatch (DWC 76, SHJ 125 min) needs your approver decision now. BAH has no road, C12 ends 09:10 — if it drops, we need a positioning flight, not standby bus.

Crew calls verified: C07 46, C15 69, C10 84 min left — all under 90, expiring pre-09:30 lift. Escalated to duty manager: S1/S2 road dispatch needs approver now; BAH has no road, so C12 (ends 09:10) needs a positioning flight if it drops.
Duty manager to crew control: hold S1/S2 buses ready for approver decision; note C12 BAH has no road and may need a positioning flight if it drops.

Picture: lift 09:30, 4885 guests stuck, 16 aircraft; 4 flights (FT 721, 006, 610, 893) already need fresh crews. Approver options: (1) dispatch standby S1/S2 by road now (DWC 76, SHJ 125 min) to cover C07/C10/C15, all expiring pre-lift; (2) position flight for C12 at BAH, no road. Framing both for decision now.

Confirmed: S1/S2 buses held at HUB pending approver; road times DWC 76, SHJ 125 min. BAH: C12 ends 09:10, currently legal with 132 min; no road exists, so if it drops we need a positioning flight — flagged.
Buses relieve C07, C15, C10 before they time out; they rest on the spot, no pressure to extend duty. Risk: buses drive through 150 m fog; C12 BAH still needs a positioning flight.
Best guests protected and cost; only risk is standby buses driving in 150 m fog and C12 BAH still needs a positioning flight.
B returns all 16 aircraft: first landings 09:30-09:42, fresh-crew flights slot into the afternoon bank from 10:48. Cancelling strips four aircraft from the bank. Risk: buses drive through 150 m fog.
Best guest outcome: 3525 protected vs 2714, 159 min shorter delays, no cancellations. Risk: buses run through 150 m fog and C07 has only 46 min slack if a standby is late.

S1/S2/S3 have 542-572 min duty left, fully fresh — no fatigue risk flying home; keeps C07/C15/C10 (39-77 min left) from being pushed. Risk: buses drive through 150 m fog, so dispatch needs careful timing; C12 BAH still needs a positioning flight.

Reopening flow (20/hr, staggered landings) handles all 16 arrivals; B rests three expiring crews and protects 3525 guests. Risk I own: buses run through 150 m fog — route and speed controls needed. C12 BAH still uncovered.
B rests C07/C15/C10 on the spot; A forces them to extend duty to fly home, and C strands crews too. Risk: C07's 46 min slack if a standby is late.
Reopening flow handles all 16 arrivals; B rests expiring crews. I own fog-road risk: staged dispatch, speed controls; C07's 46-min slack is the real exposure.
Best guests and cost, no cancellations, crews stay legal. Risk I own: C07 only 46-min slack, so buses must dispatch now; fog speed controls; C12 BAH needs positioning flight.
S1/S2/S3 fully fresh (542-572 min), C07/C15/C10 at 46-84 min must not be pushed. Fog-road timing is the risk: dispatch buses immediately, no slack. C12 BAH still needs positioning flight.
B protects 3525 guests, cuts delays 159 min, cancels none; A strands 811 more guests 264 min. Risk: fog driving; C12 BAH still needs positioning flight.
Recovery flow returns all 16 aircraft; cancelled plan strips four from the afternoon bank. Risk: bus fog delays strand C07's 46 min slack.
Plan B favored; confirm bus dispatch timing can protect C07's 46-min slack once approved.

B is safest (96%) and best overall: all 16 aircraft return, 3525 guests protected, no cancellations, no fatigue risk. Risks I'll manage: fog-speed bus controls and C12 BAH positioning. Your approval needed to proceed.
Plan B approved: S1/S2 (76 min to DWC) and S3 (125 min to SHJ) go by road to relieve C07/C15/C10; confirm arrival relief and fog timing.
Plan B approved: dispatch S1 and S2 to DWC and S3 to SHJ now; fog speed controls active, protect C07's 46-min slack, and arrange C12 BAH positioning flight.

Plan B approved: S1/S2 (76 min to DWC), S3 (125 min to SHJ) dispatched by road to relieve C07/C15/C10 under fog speed controls. Next: hotline confirms relief on arrival, then C12 BAH positioning flight.

3525 guests protected, delays down 159 min, no cancellations. Standby buses S1/S2→DWC and S3→SHJ dispatched to Crew Control; C12 BAH positioning flagged for them. Fog road timing remains the risk to C07's 46-min slack.
07:26, fog to 09:30. Crews need relief now: S1/S2 to DWC and S3 to SHJ already dispatched by road; C12 still needs a BAH positioning flight, and hub stays closed until then.
Hotline update: C07 at DWC only 11 duty min left (ends 07:37), C15 34, C10 at SHJ 49; fog lifts 09:30, so S1/S2 arrival at DWC must beat 07:37 for C07 or relieve on ground only. Confirm bus ETAs.

Crews need urgent relief: C07 at DWC has just 11 duty minutes left (ends 07:37), C15 34, C10 at SHJ 49 — all in caution. Fog lifts 09:30; C12 at BAH still needs its positioning flight. Relayed to Crew Control.
Buses arrive DWC ~08:42 and SHJ ~09:31, after C07 (07:37), C15 (08:00) and C10 limits; request ground-relief-only handling and approval for relief duties.

Hotline: road ETAs confirmed — 76 min to DWC (~08:42), 125 to SHJ (~09:31); all miss C07's 07:37, C15's 08:00 and C10's limit, so relieve on ground only at DWC and I've asked the Duty Manager to approve ground-relief handling.

C07, C15 and C10 have all timed out (0 min left). DWC legal cover: C01/C05/C02/C11; SHJ: C03/C06/C14. Buses arrive after limits, so please approve ground-relief duties for the timed-out crews and assign the legal crews to fly those aircraft home after fog clears 09:30.
C07, C15, C10 have all timed out (0 min); buses arrive 08:42/09:31, so relief is ground-only. Legal to fly home: at DWC C01/C05/C02/C11, at SHJ C03/C06/C14 — handed to Ops Duty Manager for approval.

Ground-relief for timed-out crews needs the human approver — I can't approve myself. I'm framing the option now: extend C07/C15/C10 on ground relief, then DWC C01/C05/C02/C11 and SHJ C03/C06/C14 fly the aircraft home after fog clears 09:30; escalate for approval.

Reopening wave: first landings FT721 09:30, FT006 09:33, FT455 09:36, FT610 09:39, FT918 09:42; 20/hr rate, 16 aircraft. Gates/stands ready for 09:30 onward, FT893 BAH still needs fresh crew for 11:15 dep.

Fog lifting: 16 aircraft inbound, 20 arrivals/hr. First slots: FT 721 09:30, FT 006 09:33, FT 610 09:39, FT 455 09:36, FT 918 09:42. Stands and turnaround teams ready; 7168 guests stuck, FT 893 waits fresh crew to 12:30.

Recovery check done: 16 aircraft inbound at 20/hour, first landings FT721 09:30, FT006 09:33, FT455 09:36, FT610 09:39, FT918 09:42. Hub-control asked to ready gates from 09:30; FT893 BAH still needs a fresh crew for its 11:15 departure, and 7168 guests remain stuck.
Recovery on track: 6 landed, 9 airborne with crews; only FT893 BAH still needs a fresh crew for 11:15 dep, lands 12:30.
Progress: 6 of 16 landed, 9 airborne with crews; next landings 09:48 to 10:18. Only FT893 (BAH) still needs a fresh crew, departing 11:15, landing 12:30. Guests stuck down to 4395.
FT893 BAH: C12 there is illegal (0 min, ends 09:10); legal standby S1/S2 at hub (373 min) and S3 (403) available for the 11:15 dep via positioning flight — please assign.
Acknowledged, recovery on track. FT893's local crew C12 at BAH is illegal (0 min), but standby crews S1/S2/S3 at hub are legal with 373–403 min left — passed to Crew Control for assignment.

Guests stuck down to 4395. Timed-out crews C07/C15/C10 get ground relief, pending human approval; legal crews C01/C05/C02/C11 (DWC) and C03/C06/C14 (SHJ) fly aircraft home; FT893 crew assignment escalated.

1716 guests still stuck — 280 at BAH on one diversion, rest awaiting wave arrivals; rebooking and welfare running as aircraft land 10:18 and 12:30. Two crews away from hub: C16 inbound on FT559 and FT893 awaiting fresh crew, both being covered.

Only FT893 (BAH) still needs a fresh crew — its crew covers it with a positioning flight for the 11:15 departure, landing 12:30. BAH's C12 is illegal (0 min, out at 09:10); standbys S1/S2 (299 min) and S3 (329) are legal, none under 90.

15 of 16 aircraft home at 12:01, hub open, visibility 6000 m. Guests stuck down to 280 at BAH. Only open item: FT893, fresh crew departs 11:15, lands 12:30. Lesson: keep legal standby crews positioned at outstations like BAH during fog alerts.

verdict.reason: Safety first: B 96% is clearly the safest; A 2%, C 2% dropped.
